summary.text: The Mohs scale ranks minerals from 1 to 10 by scratch resistance, based on harder material being able to scratch softer material.
Friedrich Mohs introduced it in 1812, setting diamond, the hardest known natural mineral at the time, at the top as 10.
It is an ordinal scale, so its steps are not equal: diamond is about four times as hard as corundum, which sits at 9.

facts.label: Field use
facts.value: Scratch kits for rough mineral identification

facts.label: Ancient roots
facts.value: Scratch comparisons noted by Theophrastus, c. 300 BC

items.prompt: An unknown material is scratched by apatite (rated 5) but not by fluorite (rated 4). Where does it sit on the Mohs scale?

options.label: Below 4
Above 5
Between 4 and 5
Exactly 4.5

items.explain: Hardness is set by what a material can scratch and what can scratch it, so this one falls between fluorite and apatite.

items.prompt: Corundum is 9 on the Mohs scale and diamond is 10. In absolute hardness, how do they compare?

options.label: Diamond is about 10% harder
Diamond is about four times as hard
Diamond is exactly one unit harder
They are almost equally hard

items.explain: The scale only ranks order; measured absolute hardness shows diamond about four times as hard as corundum.

items.prompt: Some sources give granite a single Mohs value between 6 and 7. Why can that number mislead?

options.label: Granite is too soft to be tested
Granite changes hardness when wet
Rocks are only rated by weight
It mixes minerals of differing hardness

items.explain: Granite is a rock made of several minerals, each with its own Mohs hardness, so one number hides that mix.

items.prompt: A softer mineral leaves permanent marks on a harder one that can only be seen under a microscope. Do these count as scratches for the Mohs test?

options.label: No, only marks visible to the naked eye count
Yes, any permanent mark counts
Yes, but only if the marks weaken it
No, only diamond can make real marks

items.explain: For the Mohs scale a scratch means a non-elastic dislocation visible to the naked eye; microscopic ones are not counted.

items.prompt: An engineer wants to predict how long a material will hold up under heavy industrial use. Is its Mohs number a good guide?

options.label: Yes, it measures wear directly
Yes, each step doubles the lifespan
No, it does not predict that well
Only if the material is a metal

items.explain: The scale helps identify minerals in the field but is not an accurate predictor of how materials endure in industry.

items.prompt: Why did diamond end up at the very top of the Mohs scale?

options.label: It was the most valuable gem known
It is ten times as hard as talc
It was the densest mineral known
It was the hardest known natural mineral

items.explain: When the scale was designed, diamond was the hardest known naturally occurring mineral, so it was arbitrarily set at 10.
